seg_under_over_segmentation — SEGMENTATION score op

• Data kinds: labels2d × labels2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.seg_under_over_segmentation(labels_pred, labels_true, *, background: 'int' = 0) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import segeval; segeval.seg_under_over_segmentation(labels_pred, labels_true, *, background: 'int' = 0) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("seg_under_over_segmentation"))

Usage

Counts over- and under-segmentation as the multiplicity of the contingency-table majority vote (Levine & Nazif style) (seg_under_over_segmentation).

Each prediction (other than background) is assigned to the true object it overlaps most (background is also a candidate). The number k_i of predictions assigned to true i is pieces_per_true, over = Σ max(k_i − 1, 0) (into how many pieces 1 true object was split). Each true object is assigned to the prediction it overlaps most, and the number m_j of true objects assigned to prediction j is objects_per_pred, under = Σ max(m_j − 1, 0) (how many true objects 1 prediction swallowed). Predictions assigned to background count as spurious (false), true objects assigned to background as missed (missing).

Returns: over, under, spurious, missed, labels_true / pieces_per_true, labels_pred / objects_per_pred, over_segmented_true (true labels with k ≥ 2), under_segmented_pred (predicted labels with m ≥ 2).
